pharm: Antineoplastic - oral VEGF receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitor
quick: 5 mg orally twice daily (about 12 hours apart), titrated by tolerability
May be taken with or without food; swallow whole with water
Avoid - can cause fetal harm; use effective contraception
Avoid during and for 2 weeks after the final dose
No adjustment for mild-moderate; limited data in severe/ESRD
Moderate (Child-Pugh B): reduce starting dose by ~half; avoid in severe
Blood pressure, thyroid function, proteinuria, LFTs, bleeding/wound healing
summary: Axitinib is an oral tyrosine kinase inhibitor that potently blocks vascular endothelial growth factor receptors (VEGFR-1, -2, -3), used to treat advanced renal cell carcinoma, alone after failure of one prior systemic therapy or in the first line combined with avelumab or pembrolizumab. Dosing starts at 5 mg twice daily and is titrated to tolerability. Hypertension (including hypertensive crisis) and hemorrhage are characteristic risks, along with thromboembolism, GI perforation, thyroid dysfunction, and impaired wound healing.
indications: First-line treatment of advanced renal cell carcinoma (RCC) in combination with avelumab
First-line treatment of advanced RCC in combination with pembrolizumab
Treatment of advanced RCC as a single agent after failure of one prior systemic therapy

dosage.d: 5 mg twice daily (avelumab 800 mg every 2 weeks)
5 mg twice daily (pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w or 400 mg q6w)

dosage.c: Advanced RCC - single agent (after prior therapy)
dosage.d: Start 5 mg twice daily; if tolerated >=2 weeks (no >40/90 BP, no antihypertensive need), increase to 7 mg then 10 mg twice daily
dosage.n: Reduce stepwise to 3 mg then 2 mg twice daily for toxicity
Resume prior dose when the inhibitor is stopped

dosage.d: Reduce the starting dose by approximately half
dosage.n: Not studied in severe (Child-Pugh C) - avoid

admin: Take doses approximately 12 hours apart, with or without food
Swallow tablets whole with a glass of water; do not crush or split
Control blood pressure before starting and monitor during treatment
Stop at least 24 hours (some protocols 2-7 days) before elective surgery and resume after adequate wound healing
Avoid grapefruit and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors/inducers where possible
moa: Axitinib is a potent and selective small-molecule inhibitor of vascular endothelial growth factor receptors VEGFR-1, VEGFR-2, and VEGFR-3. By blocking these receptor tyrosine kinases, it inhibits VEGF-mediated endothelial cell proliferation and survival, thereby suppressing tumor angiogenesis and the vascular supply that solid tumors such as renal cell carcinoma depend on for growth.

absolute: None listed in labeling (use governed by warnings/precautions)
relative: Recent arterial or venous thromboembolic event
monitor: Signs of bleeding, thrombosis, GI perforation/fistula, and wound healing

preg: Axitinib can cause fetal harm. Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose; avoid in pregnancy.
lact: Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in the breastfed child, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for 2 weeks after the final dose.
renal: No starting-dose adjustment is needed for mild to moderate renal impairment. There are limited data in severe renal impairment and end-stage renal disease; use with caution.
hepatic: For moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh B), reduce the starting dose by approximately half. Axitinib has not been studied in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C) and should be avoided.

major: Strong CYP3A4/5 inhibitors (ketoconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin, ritonavir, grapefruit) - increase axitinib levels; avoid or reduce dose by ~half
Strong CYP3A4/5 inducers (rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital, St. John's wort) - reduce axitinib levels; avoid
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice (CYP3A4 inhibition)
interactions.diagnostics: Can raise blood pressure, alter thyroid function tests, cause proteinuria, and raise liver enzymes

serious: Arterial and venous thromboembolic events (can be fatal)

monitoring: Blood pressure - control before starting and monitor regularly
Thyroid function before and periodically during treatment
Liver function tests, especially with avelumab/pembrolizumab
Signs of bleeding, thromboembolism, GI perforation/fistula, and cardiac failure
counsel: Take it twice a day about 12 hours apart and keep all blood-pressure and blood-test appointments
Report severe headache, vision changes, chest pain, weakness/numbness, or any unusual bleeding right away
Tell your team before any surgery or dental procedure - the drug is usually stopped beforehand
Avoid grapefruit and let your doctor know about all other medicines and supplements
Use effective contraception during and after treatment and do not breastfeed
pk: Antiangiogenic effect over days to weeks; antitumor response assessed by imaging
Peak plasma concentration about 2.5-4 hours after an oral dose
pearls: Hypertension (including hypertensive crisis) is a class effect - control BP before starting and monitor closely
Hemorrhage and arterial/venous thromboembolism can be fatal; discontinue for arterial thromboembolic events
Hold before elective surgery and resume only after adequate wound healing
CYP3A4 substrate - avoid grapefruit and strong inhibitors/inducers; halve the dose if a strong inhibitor is unavoidable
missed: If you miss a dose or vomit after a dose, do not take an extra dose - take the next dose at the usual scheduled time. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: There is no specific antidote for axitinib overdose. In a study, doses above the recommended level were associated with dizziness and hypertension. Management is supportive; for suspected overdose, withhold axitinib and provide supportive care with close blood-pressure monitoring.
